item.title: Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Production Systems: Empirical Evidence, Implementation Pipelines, and Industrial Applications
item.content:encoded:
Ruoqi Geng, Cardiff University

Di Li, University of Warwick

Yang Cheng, Aalborg University

This special issue seeks empirical research on how artificial intelligence augments production technologies and decision-making in real operational contexts. The focus is on system-level evidence demonstrating how point AI solutions integrate with production data environments to form end-to-end decision workflows, addressing the implementation pipeline from business-AI alignment through data readiness to deployment and workflow embedding.

The call emphasizes empirical validation using real operational evidence such as production logs, IoT sensors, industrial case studies, and field experiments. Purely conceptual, literature-review based, or synthetic-data studies are outside scope. Submissions should demonstrate how AI is operationalized across the production decision pipeline and linked to measurable production outcomes.

Appel publié par Production Planning & Control. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-Augmented Production Planning and Control
  • Business–AI Alignment and AI Readiness Pipeline for Production Systems
  • AI-enabled Quality and Process Control
  • Agentic and Workflow-Oriented Deployment in Production
  • AI-Enabled Cyber–Physical Production Systems and Digital Twins
  • AI and Additive Manufacturing
  • AI and Blockchain for Production Systems
  • Human–AI Interaction and Organisational Transformation
  • Empirical Innovations in Data, Measurement, and Evaluation
  • Extended Production Contexts (Production-Adjacent Physical Operations)

item.title: Grounded in Causality: Elevating Evidence for Leadership Practice
item.content:encoded:
This special issue of The Leadership Quarterly seeks empirical research that advances our understanding of leadership through rigorous causal inference methods. We invite submissions that employ experimental designs, quasi-experimental approaches, longitudinal studies, or other methodologically sound approaches to establish causal relationships in leadership phenomena.

item.title: Studies of Auditing "On-the-Ground" in the Majority World
item.content:encoded:
This special issue invites submissions that provide on-the-ground empirical studies of auditing practices, processes, and institutions in the Majority World countries. We welcome research that examines auditing as it is actually practiced in real-world contexts, moving beyond theoretical frameworks to understand the lived experiences of auditors, audit clients, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Appel publié par Critical Perspectives on Accounting. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
